key_insight: Watermarks can be applied more effectively and efficiently inside a generative model's latent space rather than in pixel space; DistSeal is a unified, post-hoc latent watermarking method that works across diffusion and autoregressive models.
problem_solved: Pixel-space watermarking of AI images is computationally costly and can introduce visible artifacts; there is a need for a model-agnostic, low-overhead, robust watermarking technique that can be applied to pretrained generative models without retraining them.
method: Train lightweight post-hoc watermarking networks that operate in the generative model's latent space (encode -> watermark latent -> decode).
Design objectives that balance imperceptibility (minimal visual change) and detectability/robustness so the watermark survives generation and common perturbations.
Make the approach model-agnostic and compatible with both diffusion and autoregressive pipelines by working at the shared latent representation level.
impact: Enables practitioners to add reliable, low-cost provenance signals to outputs from pretrained generative models with fewer visual artifacts and less compute than pixel-space methods — improving content traceability and stewardship.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: encoder -> latent watermark module (DistSeal) -> decoder, annotated for diffusion and autoregressive flows.
Side-by-side image comparison: original, pixel-space watermark (visible artifacts), latent-space watermark (imperceptible).
Bar chart or table: compute/time and artifact-score comparison between pixel-space vs. latent-space watermarking.
Robustness plot: detection accuracy vs. common perturbations (compression, cropping, noise) for DistSeal.
paper_title: Learning to Watermark in the Latent Space of Generative Models
paper_authors: Sylvestre-Alvise Rebuffi, Tuan Tran, Valeriu Lacatusu, Pierre Fernandez, Tomáš Souček
